claim: Ovadia et al. find that the quality of predictive uncertainty (calibration) degrades along with accuracy as dataset shift intensity increases, across all seven benchmarked UQ methods.
stance_target: N4: whether ensembles are 'confidently wrong far from the data' vs. whether calibration and accuracy degrade together under shift
scope_conditions: Classification tasks: MNIST (rotation/translation), CIFAR-10-C, ImageNet-C corruption benchmarks, Criteo click-prediction, 20 Newsgroups text classification, genomic sequence OOD detection
quoted_support: Along with accuracy, the quality of uncertainty consistently degrades with increasing dataset shift regardless of method.

claim: The paper's sole use of the phrase 'confidently wrong' describes 'most methods' in aggregate on MNIST OOD data, and explicitly attributes the least confidently-wrong behavior to SVI, not to deep ensembles.
stance_target: Claim that Ovadia et al. establishes deep ensembles specifically are 'confidently wrong far from the data'
scope_conditions: MNIST rotated/translated shift with Not-MNIST as fully-OOD dataset
quoted_support: Most methods demonstrate very low entropy (Figure 1(e)) and give high confidence predictions (Figure 1(f)) on data that is entirely OOD, i.e. they are confidently wrong about completely OOD data.

claim: On CIFAR-10/ImageNet OOD experiments (SVHN as OOD set), deep ensembles show high entropy (appropriate uncertainty) on OOD data, contradicting a 'confidently wrong' characterization of ensembles specifically.
stance_target: Claim that deep ensembles remain confidently wrong far from training data
scope_conditions: CIFAR-10 and ImageNet classifiers evaluated on SVHN as fully-OOD dataset
quoted_support: Ensembles consistently have high accuracy but also high entropy on OOD data.

claim: The paper never uses geometric/spatial distance language ('distance', 'far from', 'far away' all return zero hits); its notion of departure from training data is operationalized entirely as synthetic corruption/covariate-shift intensity or as a categorically different OOD dataset.
stance_target: Whether Ovadia et al.'s notion of 'away from the data' is geometric/spatial vs. distributional/covariate-shift
quoted_support: On the completely OOD data, one would expect the predictive distributions to be of high entropy... we would like the predictions to indicate that a model "knows what it does not know" due to the inputs straying away from the training data distribution.

claim: The paper compares against a last-layer Variational Gaussian Process only as one of eight benchmarked methods in an appendix experiment on CIFAR-10, not as its proposed or endorsed explanatory mechanism; full (non-last-layer) GPs were excluded from the main comparison as too costly to train at scale.
stance_target: Whether Ovadia et al. treats GP posterior-variance-grows-with-distance as the mechanism explaining ensemble behavior under shift
scope_conditions: Appendix E, Fig. S10, CIFAR-10 with skew intensity 0-5
quoted_support: The methods used scale well for training and prediction... We also explored methods such as scalable extensions of Gaussian Processes (Hensman et al., 2015), but they were challenging to train on the 37M example Criteo dataset or the 1000 classes of ImageNet.

claim: Bayesian optimization appears in this paper only as the hyperparameter-tuning method (Google Vizier) used to tune the classifiers under study; the terms 'acquisition', 'trust region', and 'LCB'/'lower confidence bound' do not appear at all, confirming this is a pure UQ-benchmarking paper with no engagement with Bayesian optimization or offline optimization as an application.
stance_target: Scope check: is Ovadia et al. an optimization paper or a pure UQ-benchmarking paper
quoted_support: Hyperparameters were tuned for all methods using Bayesian optimization (Golovin et al., 2017)
numbers: 3 hits for 'Bayesian optimization' (all re: hyperparameter tuning)

claim: Post-hoc temperature scaling calibration, though well-calibrated in-distribution, systematically fails under dataset shift and can even underperform an uncalibrated 'Vanilla' baseline at high shift.
stance_target: General claim that i.i.d. calibration does not transfer to shifted/OOD settings
quoted_support: Strikingly, temperature scaling has a worse Brier score than Vanilla indicating that post-hoc calibration on the validation set actually harms calibration under dataset shift.

claim: Deep ensembles are reported as the best-performing UQ method overall on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet across metrics and more robust to dataset shift, though the relative ranking of methods differs on MNIST (where SVI performs best).
stance_target: N4: ensembles' relative robustness under shift (a weaker, comparative claim, distinct from 'confidently wrong far from data')
scope_conditions: CIFAR-10 and ImageNet corruption benchmarks vs. MNIST rotation/translation benchmark
quoted_support: Deep ensembles seem to perform the best across most metrics and be more robust to dataset shift. We found that relatively small ensemble size (e.g. M = 5) may be sufficient
